To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
community financing is a promising way to improve access and financial protection for the poor.

(a) Community health financing schemes have been shown in a number of countries to improve access by rural and low income populations to needed health services, and to provide some financial protection against illness; (b) Community health financing is a promising strategy for improving access to health services and for reducing poverty, and is a strategy that can be used to strengthen the formal health sector; and (c) The success of community financing schemes depends on the ability of governments to provide a supportive policy and regulatory environment and
community financing schemes are a promising approach for improving access to health care for the poor and informal sector in developing countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how community financing can help the poor to meet their health care costs, and the extent to which it can be made sustainable and effective in the long run.
the question of how to finance and provide heath care to the more than 3.3 billion people in low and middle-income countries who live on less than US$2 per day.
the question of how to improve the effectiveness of community financing schemes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
community financing can be an effective and sustainable mechanism to improve access and financial risk protection for the informal sector and rural poor.
community financing schemes are a useful tool to improve the access and financial protection of the poor and informal workers to health care.

the available evidence indicates that community financing can improve access and financial protection, but that the effectiveness and sustainability depends critically on the quality of the enabling environment, and on the quality of management of the community based health insurance schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
community financing is a useful tool to help meet the health care needs of the poor and the informal sector.
community financing can make a positive difference to health outcomes and equity, but that it is not a panacea for the problems of financing health care in poor countries.
there is no single model of community financing that will work for every country.
The main takeaway from our work is that

community financing schemes can make important contributions to the health care financing challenge in low and middle countries if they are well managed and supported by appropriate government policies.
the community financing approach is a viable option for the financing and delivery of health care to the more than 2 billion people who are excluded from the formal financing and delivery system.
the community financing approach is a useful and effective tool to meet the health needs of the rural poor and informal workers in low and midle income countries.
